patch_description: The original program returned random points (score ~0.01, min area ~0). Instead of random placement, I implement a deterministic annealed hill-climbing optimizer: it starts from a convex-position configuration (points near a circle, which avoids degenerate collinear triples), then iteratively perturbs single points with a geometrically decaying step size, accepting moves that increase the objective — the minimum triangle area normalized by the convex hull area. The objective is evaluated with a fully vectorized NumPy computation over all 286 point triples, making thousands of iterations fast. Key insights used: optimal Heilbronn configurations tend toward convex position (interior points create small triangles), scale invariance lets the objective be the ratio min-triangle-area / hull-area, and coordinate descent with annealing provides robust local refinement from a well-chosen structured start. A fixed seed guarantees reproducibility.
